# Checkly — Style Reference

> Blueprint vellum over a server-room console, one cobalt pilot light. Inter at weight 500 with tight negative tracking, terminal mono carrying the story, a #041734 navy canvas, 1px steel-blue rules at 20% and a single cobalt word.

**Theme:** dark

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Checkly speaks a terminal-blueprint product language. The page is assembled from its own CLI output, code editors and dashboards, and the monospace face logs 360 measured uses against 238 for regular Inter. The canvas is Ink Canvas #041734. Mockup panels sink into Carbon Panel #0a1929 and Jet Well #001027, and raised tiles lift on Frosted Glass #ffffff0d. The chromatic budget is one brand hue plus a status triad. Cobalt Signal #0075ff is rationed to a single headline word, eyebrows and links. Moss Pulse #2ea45d, Ember Alert #ef4444 and Sunshine Warn #eab308 live only inside product mockups. Inter at weight 500 sets every heading, tightened to -0.04em at 36px and 48px with a Perfect Fourth step between them. Hierarchy comes from size and from Paper-versus-Fog color, not from weight. Shapes are soft, with 8px buttons and 12px windows. Depth comes from 1px Steel Hairline #6094c133 rules, and shadows are reserved for floating windows. The result reads as an operations console rather than a marketing brochure.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ink Canvas | `#041734` | `--color-ink-canvas` | Page background, footer fill and the label color on the Paper CTA — a blue-black navy instead of the conventional #000 or #0a0a0a gives the dark theme a blueprint temperature. |
| Jet Well | `#001027` | `--color-jet-well` | Copy-icon buttons, inset command wells and the deepest mockup recesses — it sits darker than the canvas, so inset controls read as cut into the page (5 uses). |
| Carbon Panel | `#0a1929` | `--color-carbon-panel` | Terminal window bodies, the code editor and dashboard mockups — a desaturated near-black that separates product UI from the bluer marketing canvas. |
| Frosted Glass | `#ffffff0d` | `--color-frosted-glass` | Raised tiles, chat bubbles and the active logo tab — a 5% white veil (40 uses, plus 30 at 3%) that elevates by tint rather than shadow. |
| Ash Comment | `#445458` | `--color-ash-comment` | Code line numbers, commented code and disabled meta inside mockups (77 uses) — the terminal's dim register. Do not use it for body copy, because it fails contrast on #041734. |
| Fog Caption | `#a7babe` | `--color-fog-caption` | Hero subcopy, feature descriptions and logo-strip intro (134 uses) — a cool grey-green that pushes paragraphs one step behind white headings. |
| Paper | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper` | Headlines, nav links and the solid CTA fill (110 text uses) — the brightest value on the page doubles as the action color. Do not tint it blue for buttons. |
| Steel Hairline | `#6094c133` | `--color-steel-hairline` | Section rules, the feature-column grid and window outlines (68 uses) — a 20% steel-blue 1px line that draws the blueprint and replaces most shadows. |
| Cobalt Signal | `#0075ff` | `--color-cobalt-signal` | The word "active" in the H1, uppercase eyebrows and text links (25 uses) — the only brand hue, kept as punctuation rather than decoration. Do not promote it to the primary CTA fill. |
| Moss Pulse | `#2ea45d` | `--color-moss-pulse` | Passing-check bars, status dots and sparkline fills (49 background uses, the top saturated count) — the meaning is "healthy", so it stays inside mockups and status chips. |
| Mint Pulse | `#4ade80` | `--color-mint-pulse` | "Available" and "All passing" labels and success lines in terminal output (26 uses) — Moss Pulse lightened for legible text on navy. |
| Ember Alert | `#ef4444` | `--color-ember-alert` | The failing region tile, error dots and the red window-chrome light (32 uses) — the incident color. Do not use it for marketing emphasis. |
| Sunshine Warn | `#eab308` | `--color-sunshine-warn` | Degraded-state dots and the amber window-chrome light (24 uses) — completes the traffic-light triad and stays out of copy and CTAs. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Inter — display, UI and body sans at a single medium voice · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter from Google Fonts at 500 for headings and 400 for body (the same face, so it matches exactly), Geist at 500 (draws a touch lighter, so stay at 500 rather than 400), Hanken Grotesk at 500 (slightly narrower, with the same stroke).
- **Weights:** 300, 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 8px, 9px, 10px, 10.5px, 11px, 14px, 16px, 20px, 36px, 48px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.11, 1.4, 1.43, 1.45, 1.5, 1.625
- **Letter spacing:** -1.92px at 48px, -1.44px at 36px, -0.8px on one 20px heading, -0.35px at 14px uppercase eyebrows, 0px everywhere else
- **Role:** Weight 500 at 48px is the headline decision. Most dev-tool landing pages push Inter display to 600 or 700, and this one stays a step lighter, so headlines read as stated fact rather than shouted claims. The -0.04em tracking at 36px and 48px tightens the face toward a display cut. The 48/36 pair is a Perfect Fourth (1.333), while 20/16 is a Major Third (1.25). The scale is therefore steep at the top and flat in the body band, which hands the micro sizes (8–11px) to mockup chrome.

### ui-monospace — terminal output, code and data labels; the most-used face on the page · `--font-ui-monospace`

- **Substitute:** Geist Mono at 400, JetBrains Mono at 350 (its 400 draws heavier and wider than SF Mono, so drop it a step to match the stroke), IBM Plex Mono at 400.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 9px, 10px, 10.5px, 11px, 12px, 14px
- **Line height:** 1.33, 1.375, 1.5, 1.6, 1.625
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at all sizes
- **Role:** With 360 uses, the mono face outnumbers every Inter weight. That is the anti-convention core of the system, because the product's own CLI is the illustration. The 12px size at 1.625 leading (184 uses) is the workhorse caption, and 700 appears only for check names and command prompts. Untracked mono beside tightly tracked Inter is the pairing: Inter is the narrator and mono is the evidence.

### -apple-system — system UI inside mockup chrome · `--font-apple-system`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 400, Roboto at 400, Source Sans 3 at 400 (it reads slightly lighter, so use 500 for labels).
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 10px, 12px
- **Line height:** 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** 0px
- **Role:** This face appears only inside product reconstructions such as dashboard rows, filter chips and window titles. There it imitates native app chrome rather than marketing type. Treat it as mockup-internal, and do not set marketing copy in it.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Inter | 400 | 9px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | ui-monospace | 400 | 12px | 1.625 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter | 400 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| subheading | Inter | 500 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Inter | 500 | 20px | 1.4 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Inter | 500 | 36px | 1.11 | -1.44px | `--text-heading` |
| display | Inter | 500 | 48px | 1 | -1.92px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every heading in Inter weight 500 with -0.04em tracking (-1.92px at 48px, -1.44px at 36px) — the medium weight keeps claims declarative while the tracking supplies density.
- Build feature proof from mockups on #0a1929 with ui-monospace 12px at 1.625 leading — the product's own terminal is the illustration, and mono should outnumber the sans.
- Fill the primary action with #ffffff and label it #041734 at 8px radius and 8px 20px padding — the brightest neutral wins attention without spending the accent.
- Ration Cobalt Signal #0075ff to one headline word, eyebrows and links — at 25 uses against 110 white text uses, cobalt stays a signal.
- Divide sections with 1px #6094c133 rules that bleed to the viewport edges — the blueprint grid carries structure that cards would otherwise need.
- Keep status hues (#2ea45d, #ef4444, #eab308) inside mockups and status pills — they mean pass, fail and degraded, and that semantic contract is non-negotiable.
- Separate sections by 96px and cap paragraph measures at 672px — generous vertical air offsets the dense 12px mono inside the panels.

### Don't

- Don't bold headlines to 700 — weight 700 appears only 8 times in Inter, and bold display turns the restrained console voice into a sales banner.
- Don't make the CTA cobalt #0075ff — a blue button competes with the single blue headline word and collapses the one-accent budget.
- Don't replace the product mockups with abstract illustrations, 3D orbs or stock photography — the terminal output is the thesis, and decorative art makes the page read like any other SaaS hero.
- Don't use pure #000000 for the canvas — the #041734 navy is what gives the hairlines at 20% their blueprint tint, and black turns them grey.
- Don't put `--shadow-lg` on every card — real shadows belong to floating windows, while ruled columns stay flat on 1px #6094c133.
- Don't set body copy in #445458 — on #041734 it fails contrast, and its job is dim code comments and line numbers.
- Don't round feature columns to 12px or above — ruled cells have no radius, and rounding them turns the spec-sheet grid into a stack of floating cards.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #041734 (Ink Canvas)
- panel surface: #0a1929 (Carbon Panel)
- primary text: #ffffff (Paper)
- secondary text: #a7babe (Fog Caption)
- hairline: #6094c133 (Steel Hairline)
- accent: #0075ff (Cobalt Signal)
- status pass: #2ea45d (Moss Pulse)
- primary action: #ffffff (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts use solid #2ea45d bars for passing results, solid #ef4444 or #eab308 only for failed or degraded data points, and neutral #a7babe or #445458 for axes and labels. Cobalt #0075ff is limited to the single selected series or active page indicator, so data never outshouts the headline.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button labeled "Start for free": background #ffffff, text #041734, 1px solid #ffffff border, border-radius 8px, padding 8px 20px, Inter 16px weight 500 with 24px line height (resulting height 42px), no shadow. Pair it with a ghost twin labeled "Book a demo" with a transparent background, #ffffff text and a 1px solid #ffffff border, using identical radius and padding, with a 12px gap between them, both on a #041734 canvas.

2. Build a hero section on #041734 inside a 1536px container, split into two columns with a 48px gap. Left column: an H1 in Inter 48px weight 500, line height 1, letter-spacing -1.92px, color #ffffff, with one word colored #0075ff. Then a 16px weight 400 paragraph in #a7babe at line height 1.5, max-width 512px, 24px below the H1. Then the button pair 32px below. Then a command chip 16px below reading `npx checkly init` in ui-monospace 14px #ffffff, 1px #6094c133 border, 4px radius, 12px 16px padding, with a 44px #001027 copy button at 4px radius. Right column: stacked terminal windows.

3. Build a Terminal Window Card: background #0a1929, 1px solid #6094c133 border, border-radius 12px, box-shadow `0px 2px 4px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.1), 0px 8px 24px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.18), 0px 32px 72px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.32)`. Add a title bar with 12px padding containing three 8px circles (#ef4444, #eab308 and a mockup green) with 6px gaps, plus a ui-monospace 12px label in #a7babe. Body padding is 16px with ui-monospace 12px at line height 1.625: a `$` prompt in #445458, commands in #ffffff, and success lines prefixed with a check mark in #4ade80.

4. Build a sticky navigation bar 78px tall, background #041734, no border, no shadow, content constrained to 1536px. Left: the wordmark, then links in Inter 14px weight 400 #ffffff with 10px 16px padding and an 8px-radius hover plate of #ffffff0d. Four links carry 12px chevrons. Right: a "Login" link in the same style, then a Paper button (#ffffff background, #041734 text, Inter 14px weight 500, 8px 20px padding, 8px radius), separated by a 12px gap.

5. Build a grid-ruled feature row: three equal columns separated by 1px solid #6094c133 vertical rules, with horizontal 1px #6094c133 rules above and below extending to the full viewport width. Give each cell 24px 12px padding, no background and no radius. Set the heading in Inter 20px weight 500, line height 1.4, #ffffff, and the 8px-gapped body in Inter 16px weight 400, line height 1.5, #a7babe. Below each, a flush #0a1929 mockup clipped by the next rule.

### Solid Button — Paper (Primary)

**Role:** The single conversion action

### Navigation Bar — Sticky Dark

**Role:** Global wayfinding and persistent CTA

"Product", "Solutions", "Developers" and "Resources" carry chevrons, and "Customers" and "Pricing" have none. Each link is Inter 14px weight 400 in #ffffff with 10px 16px padding at 8px radius, so the 8px hover plate matches the button radius. "Login" and the 38px Paper button sit right. The bar has no border and no shadow, so it reads as part of the canvas rather than a floating chrome strip.

### Mobile Menu Row — Light Sheet

**Role:** Drawer navigation on small screens

This is the deliberate system outlier, a light surface. The drawer flips to a #ffffff sheet. Each row is full-width Inter 16px weight 500 in #041734 with 16px 12px padding and an 8px radius hover plate, with no border or shadow. It is allowed to break the dark canvas because a full-screen overlay needs maximum separation from the page beneath. The inversion reuses the exact Paper and Ink pair from the primary button, so no new color enters the system.

### Command Snippet Chip

**Role:** Copyable install command

This is a terminal fragment set as a button. It shows `npx checkly init` in ui-monospace 14px weight 400 #ffffff on #041734, framed by a 1px Steel Hairline #6094c133 border at 4px radius with 12px 16px padding. A 44px #001027 copy button at 4px radius anchors the right edge. Placing a shell command under the CTAs is anti-convention for a hero. It tells developers the real first step is the terminal, not a signup form.

**Role:** Primary content container for product proof

This is the main card, and every card on the page is a window. It has a #0a1929 body, a 1px #6094c133 border and 12px radius, with 16px padding and the three-layer `--shadow-lg` beneath. A title bar carries three 8px dots in #ef4444, #eab308 and a mockup-internal green, plus a 12px mono path label in #a7babe. **Role:** Three-up capability statement

This is a blueprint cell. It has no fill and no radius, and it is bounded by full-bleed 1px #6094c133 rules that run past the container to both viewport edges. Padding is 24px 12px. An Inter 20px weight 500 #ffffff heading sits over Inter 16px weight 400 #a7babe copy, and a flush Carbon Panel mockup is clipped below. **Role:** System-health indicator inline with copy

This is a heartbeat badge. It uses Moss Pulse #2ea45d at 15% opacity as the background, Mint Pulse #4ade80 text in Inter 14px weight 500 and 9999px radius. **Role:** Environment names inside prose

This is a highlighted noun. The words `test`, `staging` and `prod` are set in ui-monospace 14px weight 400 with #0075ff text on a Cobalt Signal tint at 10% (estimated), at 4px radius with 2px 6px padding. They sit on the 16px subheading baseline. Setting environment names as code tokens inside a sentence is how the terminal thesis reaches the copy layer without turning paragraphs into code blocks.

**Role:** Section kicker above headings

This is a cobalt caption. It is set in Inter 14px weight 600, uppercase, with -0.35px tracking and #0075ff text, and sits 12px above a 36px or 48px heading ("WHAT CUSTOMERS SAY", "THE PROBLEM"). **Role:** Testimonial selector by brand

This is a ruled logo index. White monochrome logos sit in cells divided by 1px #6094c133 verticals, between horizontal rules that bleed to the viewport edges. Each cell has 24px 20px padding. **Role:** AI-agent interaction mockup

This is a chat input as product proof. It has a #0a1929 shell, a 1px #6094c133 border and 8px radius with 12px padding. The textarea is Inter 14px weight 400 at 1.625 leading in Paper at 80% opacity. ## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every heading in Inter weight 500 with -0.04em tracking (-1.92px at 48px, -1.44px at 36px) — the medium weight keeps claims declarative while the tracking supplies density.
- Build feature proof from mockups on #0a1929 with ui-monospace 12px at 1.625 leading — the product's own terminal is the illustration, and mono should outnumber the sans.
- Fill the primary action with #ffffff and label it #041734 at 8px radius and 8px 20px padding — the brightest neutral wins attention without spending the accent.
- Ration Cobalt Signal #0075ff to one headline word, eyebrows and links — at 25 uses against 110 white text uses, cobalt stays a signal.
- Divide sections with 1px #6094c133 rules that bleed to the viewport edges — the blueprint grid carries structure that cards would otherwise need.
- Keep status hues (#2ea45d, #ef4444, #eab308) inside mockups and status pills — they mean pass, fail and degraded, and that semantic contract is non-negotiable.
- Separate sections by 96px and cap paragraph measures at 672px — generous vertical air offsets the dense 12px mono inside the panels.

### Don't

- Don't bold headlines to 700 — weight 700 appears only 8 times in Inter, and bold display turns the restrained console voice into a sales banner.
- Don't make the CTA cobalt #0075ff — a blue button competes with the single blue headline word and collapses the one-accent budget.
- Don't replace the product mockups with abstract illustrations, 3D orbs or stock photography — the terminal output is the thesis, and decorative art makes the page read like any other SaaS hero.
- Don't use pure #000000 for the canvas — the #041734 navy is what gives the hairlines at 20% their blueprint tint, and black turns them grey.
- Don't put `--shadow-lg` on every card — real shadows belong to floating windows, while ruled columns stay flat on 1px #6094c133.
- Don't set body copy in #445458 — on #041734 it fails contrast, and its job is dim code comments and line numbers.
- Don't round feature columns to 12px or above — ruled cells have no radius, and rounding them turns the spec-sheet grid into a stack of floating cards.

## Imagery

The page uses no photography. Every image is a reconstructed product interface: a Claude Code session, CLI test output, a TypeScript editor with syntax colors, a check dashboard with sparkline bars, and an agent chat composer. Windows sit at 12px radius on #0a1929 with a 1px #6094c133 border and the layered `--shadow-lg`. Syntax highlighting uses mockup-internal hues, including a decorative purple #a371f7 and a grey #4b5563, which are not system tokens. Icons are 14px monochrome line glyphs, and the region tiles carry flag emoji. The world map is a dot matrix drawn in 1.3px monospace characters, with #2ea45d location nodes connected to one cobalt hub. A faint cobalt underglow sits beneath the hero stack, and it is decorative only. Customer logos render as flat #ffffff marks. The narrative is that the product watches the world, and the page shows the console doing it.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1536px container, with headings capped at 768px and paragraphs at 672px. Sections are separated by 96px (64–112px), and full-bleed 1px #6094c133 rules mark band boundaries. The hero is a two-column split. The 48px headline, Fog Caption subcopy, the button pair and the command chip sit left. A vertical stack of three terminal windows sits right, fanning into four region tiles through connector lines. Sections alternate between left-aligned headline blocks and ruled mockup bands. The feature row uses three equal ruled columns, and the customer logo grid uses six columns by two rows. The testimonial logo strip runs eight ruled cells. There is no pricing grid on the home page. The nav is sticky, 78px tall and filled with #041734, with the wordmark and six links left and Login plus the Paper CTA right. The footer is a #041734 block with 96px vertical padding and multi-column uppercase-headed link lists. At 375px, drop the display to 36px, set section gaps to 64px and stack mockups below copy. The overall density is comfortable.

## Terminal-First Storytelling

The defining discipline is that the product is the illustration. Monospace logs 360 uses against 238 for regular Inter, and every visual on the page is a console, editor or dashboard the product actually ships. The system breaks the moment a section reaches for an abstract hero graphic, an isometric illustration or a stock photo. Any of those turns proof into decoration and makes the page read like a generic SaaS template. To extend it, take a new capability and render its real output on a 12px-radius #0a1929 window, set in ui-monospace 12px at 1.625 leading. Let status hues report actual state inside the mockup. Explain the panel with a single 20px weight 500 Inter heading beside it, not with an icon grid.

## Hairline Blueprint Grid

Structure is drawn, not stacked. A 1px Steel Hairline #6094c133 appears 68 times and runs past the container to both viewport edges, ruling feature columns, logo strips and testimonial bands into a spec sheet. Shadows are the exception, used on about ten floating elements. The grid breaks when ruled cells get filled backgrounds, 12px corners or drop shadows, because they become floating cards and the blueprint dissolves into a conventional bento layout. It also breaks when the hairline is raised above 20% opacity, which makes the rules louder than the content. To extend it, add new bands as ruled rows with 24px 12px cell padding. Reserve 12px radius and `--shadow-lg` for objects that represent real windows.

## Rationed Cobalt

The chromatic discipline is one brand hue. Cobalt Signal #0075ff appears on a single word of the H1, on uppercase eyebrows and on links, a total of 25 uses on a page with 110 white text uses. The status triad is semantic, not brand. The system breaks if cobalt fills the CTA, tints card backgrounds or colors chart series by default, because the one blue word in the headline then stops being the first thing the eye lands on. To extend it, give each new section at most one cobalt moment, either an eyebrow or a key word. Let #ffffff carry actions, and route all other color through pass, fail and degraded meanings inside product mockups.

## Similar Brands

- **Vercel** — The same white-filled primary button on a dark canvas with mono command snippets in the hero, though Vercel's canvas is neutral black where Checkly's is #041734 navy.
- **Linear** — Inter headings at medium weight with negative tracking and hairline-defined dark surfaces, though Linear leans on gradients and glows that Checkly limits to a single cobalt underglow.
- **Supabase** — Code-forward product storytelling with real editor and terminal mockups as hero imagery, with green as brand where Checkly confines green to status.
- **Better Stack** — A direct monitoring competitor that uses status-colored dashboards and region maps as proof, though it reads warmer and more illustrated than Checkly's ruled blueprint.
- **Grafana Labs** — Dark observability UI where pass/fail color carries data meaning, while Checkly strips the marketing layer down to one accent hue.
